name: worldquest

scripts.generate: pnpm design:tokens && pnpm i18n:types && pnpm edge:build
scripts.verify: pnpm generate && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm content:validate && pnpm i18n:check && pnpm design:contrast && pnpm lint:a11y && pnpm escape-hatches && pnpm reachability && pnpm five-states
scripts.$comment:typecheck:edge: The edge modules were the only TypeScript here nobody typechecked: Vitest transforms them with esbuild, which strips types without checking them, so `pnpm test` went green on code `tsc` rejects — and it is the code that verifies signatures and decides who has paid. Four real defects on the first run. The Deno entrypoints stay excluded; see supabase/tsconfig.json.
scripts.$comment:e2e: Exports the real bundle through Metro and drives it in Chromium via react-native-web. Not a device — see apps/mobile/e2e/flow.cjs for exactly what that does and does not prove. The export step is the point as much as the driving: it is the only thing in this repo that runs the bundler.
scripts.e2e: pnpm --filter @worldquest/mobile exec expo export --platform web --output-dir ../../node_modules/.cache/wq-web && node apps/mobile/e2e/flow.cjs node_modules/.cache/wq-web node_modules/.cache/wq-e2e-shots
scripts.$comment:design:shots: Screenshots any set of routes from the exported bundle at 320/390/768 and reports the things a picture cannot show — touch targets under 44pt, sideways scroll, unlabelled controls. Feeds /design-review. Never a gate: verify and e2e are the gates.
scripts.design:shots: pnpm --filter @worldquest/mobile exec expo export --platform web --output-dir ../../node_modules/.cache/wq-web && node scripts/design-shots.cjs
scripts.$comment:bundle:native: Bundles for iOS and Android, and enforces a per-platform size budget. Until this existed the app had only ever been bundled for web, and Metro resolves per platform — a native-only resolution failure was invisible. The budget is here because Hermes reads the whole bundle before the first frame, making size the one cold-start input measurable without a phone. Proves the graph compiles and is not growing quietly; NOT that the app runs.
scripts.$comment:build:flags: Rasterises the 65 country flags from flag-icons (MIT) into apps/mobile/assets/flags. Flags sat in the 'needs an illustrator' bucket for the whole project, which was wrong: a national flag is a public-domain drawing somebody has already got right, and drawing one from memory is the wrong-fact bug asset-prompts.md forbids. Run it when the country list changes; the PNGs are committed, so it is not part of verify.
scripts.$comment:build:maps: Projects and rasterises the region + country outlines from Natural Earth (via world-atlas, public domain) into apps/mobile/assets/geo. Map thumbnails were filed as 'needs an illustrator' for the whole project — the third time that mistake was made, after sound and flags — while asset-prompts.md listed geometry under NEVER GENERATE and named Natural Earth in the same row. Run it when the country list changes; the PNGs are committed, so it is not part of verify.
scripts.$comment:build:icons: Rasterises the UI icon set from Lucide (ISC) into apps/mobile/assets/icons as white-on-transparent alpha masks, recoloured at runtime with tintColor. The fourth false blocker after sound, flags and geometry: asset-prompts.md has named Lucide and Phosphor since it was written, while the tab bar shipped '⌂ ◎ ◈ ☺ ⋯' as literal text — a different typeface on every device, four of them colour emoji, none of them mirroring for RTL. Run it when the icon set changes; the PNGs are committed, so it is not part of verify.
scripts.$comment:build:locations: Derives facts.locations.v1.json from the `subregion` already declared on every entity, so a country's location fact can never disagree with its own entity. Invents no geography — it is a projection of data the pack holds. Run it when the country list changes; the JSON is committed, so it is not part of verify.
scripts.$comment:db:types: A script, not one line, because the committed file carries a 'do not hand-edit' header and single-quoted literals that the generator emits double-quoted — both applied by hand, once. CI ran the raw command and diffed the result, so that check compared a decorated file against an undecorated one and could never pass, however fresh the types were. The decoration now lives in the generator: one command, run by humans and by CI, whose output is exactly what is committed. --local, not --project-id: migrations are the source of truth, and the hosted project is currently a migration behind.
scripts.$comment:edge:build: Verifies the deploy bundle is self-contained AND writes its generated half — `_content/answers.ts`, the fact→entity answer key derived from the packs. Until this wrote anything, the function on disk imported a file no checkout had ever contained, so `supabase start` and `supabase functions deploy` both failed on it. Part of `generate`, so a fresh clone can start the local stack.
scripts.$comment:edge:deploy: store-notifications deploys with --no-verify-jwt because Apple is not a user and holds no JWT. That is not a weaker check: the store's own signature — a pinned chain, a per-payload ECDSA signature, and an audience check that the notification is about our bundle — is a stronger claim than a JWT is.
scripts.edge:deploy: supabase functions deploy submit-lesson --project-ref tjdjogidudjobxipibqb && supabase functions deploy store-notifications --no-verify-jwt --project-ref tjdjogidudjobxipibqb
scripts.$comment:screenshot: `.png=dataurl` rather than `file`: this harness emits ONE standalone HTML file into a cache directory and shoots it there, so a relative asset path would resolve to nothing and every flag would render blank — which looks exactly like the placeholder it replaced. Inlining costs ~900 KB in a throwaway file and cannot half-work.
scripts.screenshot: esbuild scripts/screenshot/render.tsx --bundle --platform=node --format=cjs --jsx=automatic --alias:react-native=react-native-web --define:__DEV__=false --alias:expo-linear-gradient=./scripts/screenshot/linear-gradient-web.tsx --loader:.json=json --loader:.png=dataurl --outfile=node_modules/.cache/wq-render.cjs && node node_modules/.cache/wq-render.cjs > node_modules/.cache/wq-app.html && node scripts/screenshot/shoot.cjs node_modules/.cache/wq-app.html docs/design/assets/screens
scripts.$comment:escape-hatches: Fails on `any`, @ts-expect-error, @ts-ignore or eslint-disable outside tests. PROJECT.md §12 has banned all four since week one and nothing checked — the DoD ✅ rested on nobody having broken it yet. Deliberate exceptions live in an allowlist with a written reason, and a stale entry fails the same as a violation.
scripts.$comment:a11y:tree: Walks Chromium's computed accessibility tree over ten routes — the thing a screen reader actually consumes. lint:a11y reads source and design:shots accepts textContent as a label, so a button whose only content is an emoji passed both. This is the mechanical half of the VoiceOver/TalkBack box; the manual pass in docs/plan/device-pass.md is still required.
scripts.a11y:tree: pnpm --filter @worldquest/mobile exec expo export --platform web --output-dir ../../node_modules/.cache/wq-web && node scripts/a11y-tree.cjs
